api_checks.description: Sign in with a registered email and correct password: response sets an HTTP-only session cookie (Set-Cookie header) and a subsequent authenticated request made with that cookie succeeds.

Register a new member: response is 201 with a MemberView body carrying only id and email. Assert the response body (and every field in it) contains no `password` key, no `password_hash` key, no `$argon2id$` substring, and not the plaintext password — the credential is stored, never echoed. Then POST /auth/sign-in with the same credentials returns 200, proving the stored value is a verifiable hash rather than a rejected/plaintext-compared value. The literal `$argon2id$` prefix assertion on the stored column is the unit-layer half of VM-002 (CHK-VM-002-unit, backend/tests/unit/test_auth_service.py); this api check is the runtime-observable half the matrix also requires.

Drive POST /auth/register then POST /auth/sign-in for the same member with a known plaintext password, then capture the backend service logs emitted during that request window (`docker compose logs backend` in docker mode, process stderr in local mode). Assert the captured log output contains neither the plaintext password string nor any `$argon2id$` substring for either request. This is executable at runtime by the evaluator and is the api-layer half of VM-003 (CHK-VM-003-api); CHK-VM-003-unit covers the logging_config redaction in isolation.
Sign in with an unregistered email or a wrong password: response is 401 and no session cookie is set.
With a reachable database, GET /healthz returns 200.
With the database stopped/unreachable, GET /healthz returns 503.
GET /healthz requires no authentication and returns a JSON body describing database status.

From a clean checkout with no cached project images, run `docker compose up`. The stack is healthy when GET /healthz against the composed backend returns 200 (which succeeds only if backend and Postgres are both up on the compose network). Additionally assert `docker compose ps` reports every service healthy and exactly one running container built from a `postgres:16` image.

With the stack running — liveness anchored by GET /healthz returning 200 — inspect build and runtime network traffic (image build logs and per-service egress) and assert no service makes a request to a host outside the compose network. The 200 anchor proves the stack under inspection is the running one; the egress assertion is the substance of the check.

With the stack running — liveness anchored by GET /healthz returning 200 — parse the docker-compose.yml that produced it and assert it defines exactly one Postgres 16 service and no other third-party managed service. The 200 anchor proves the parsed file is the one that booted the stack; the service-inventory assertion is the substance of the check.
